title: My little experiment with moss-covered buttons, knobs and AI-generated motion
author: mrdub
selftext:
A little personal experiment in making browser controls feel like physical objects.

**Qwen-Image 2.1** generated the panel artwork, and **MiniMax H3** generated the button and knob animations. These are for a character builder I’m working on. The flower and moss have subtle animation loops too.

Playable version: [https://lab.giantaperture.com/experiments/moss-controls/](https://lab.giantaperture.com/experiments/moss-controls/)

Curious how the controls feel to other people—especially the glass buttons and knob.

replies.body: Like an underglow from the slider trough? That sounds cool. I don't have much experience with other models outside of qwen 2.1, I do like that it is pretty direct able. Luckily, codex just grinds through it.

comments.author: kneecolesbean
comments.body: I like it.   The dial feels a little awkward because I don't seem to be able to do a full rotation in a single click, and the grab seems inconsistent.   Also I'd personally expect the light bar to be increasing if I turn it clockwise.

replies.author: mrdub
replies.body: Yes, this def needs some work to polish it, kind of playing with whether the mouse click and drag should grip it and require a rotation or just treat it like a scroll where you can click and drag down on a side to make it turn. Touch interfaces are a little easier as you can more directly tap and drag in a circular motion.

replies.author: mrdub
replies.body:
I generated the start and stop frames and directed H3 to generate the motion between the two endpoint images using first/last frame image conditioning. 

https://preview.redd.it/3e88uvovd5vh1.png?width=256&format=png&auto=webp&s=181e78f8bd0cd61247287f9fde9869686638c920

Prompt

>The inspected input image owns the exact control assembly, pose, materials, layout, camera and lighting. Animate only the explicitly requested mechanisms and local optical effects.

>Exact locked macro camera on this dark fluted rotary knob with its blank ivory top and complete stationary receiving seat. Animate the rigid grip and attached ivory top turning CLOCKWISE smoothly during the first 3.6 seconds, then hold. Small existing wear and the fluted grip highlights travel naturally with the turn; shaft, circular footprint, diameter, height and construction stay unchanged.

>The first image is the same assembly at minimum value, with the outer progress track dark. The last image gives the exact maximum-value blue progress track: a narrow blue illuminated arc on the OUTER edge of the STATIONARY circular collar, outside the grip and its contact shadow. Grow that exact blue track steadily clockwise from its fixed lower-left origin around the collar to the supplied maximum state as the knob turns. Do not illuminate the collar all at once.

>The moving grip and its ivory top never emit or acquire a stripe, notch, marker or new lamp. The fixed collar stays fixed; the receiving metal, mounting frame, screws, moss, camera, studio light and exposure stay fixed. Only the requested outer track and its restrained local reflections illuminate.

>Preserve the photographic materials, strong blue progress readability and natural contact shadow. Do not add another component or move the receiving plate. No hand or finger.

>Rigid manufactured parts retain their exact geometry and identity. Camera, mounting plate, bezel, screws, stationary markings and frost on the plate remain fixed. The fixed lighting rig and exposure remain stable. Explicitly requested local indicator emission may change, with local reflection and spill; reflections and shadows respond physically to the explicitly moving mechanisms.

>No new objects, text, hands, camera motion, panel bending, changing scale or decor
